questions.question: Which wildcard syntax do `--exclude`/`--include` globs support in zgrep? Is `[abc]` a character class?
questions.reference: matchPattern (src/filter.zig) supports only `*` and `?`, and strips a trailing `/`. There are no character classes: `[` is compared literally, so `[abc]` only matches the literal text `[abc]`. Matching is case-sensitive.

questions.question: With `--exclude-ext=log`, are the files `a.log`, `catalog`, `.log` and `A.LOG` excluded?
questions.reference: matchesExt (src/filter.zig): for an extension without a leading dot, the name must be longer than ext+1 and have a '.' right before the extension. So `a.log` is excluded; `catalog` is not (no dot before `log`); `.log` is not (length 4 is not > 4); `A.LOG` is not (case-sensitive comparison).

questions.question: Which directories does zgrep skip by default? Are `dist` or `build` among them?
questions.reference: default_excluded_dirs (src/filter.zig): .git, .zig-cache, __pycache__, node_modules, .venv, venv, target, .cache, .idea, .vscode. Neither dist nor build is in the list. --no-ignore or --no-default-ignore disable the list.

questions.question: With `-G` (basic regex), what do `a\+b`, `a+b` and a pattern starting with `*` mean?
questions.reference: breToEre (src/bre.zig) inverts the escapes: `\+` becomes the ERE operator `+` (one or more), so `a\+b` matches `ab`, `aab`...; a bare `+` becomes a literal plus, so `a+b` matches the text `a+b`; a `*` at the start of a pattern, branch or group is a literal.

questions.question: In a `--queries-file`, what values may "id" take, what happens with unknown fields, duplicate ids and blank lines, and can a bad line leave the batch half-run?
questions.reference: parseQueries (src/batch.zig): id is a string or a non-negative integer; unknown fields are rejected; a duplicate id is an error; blank lines are ignored. The whole file is parsed before anything runs (fails closed), so a bad line never leaves a batch half-run.

questions.question: How does `--max-output-tokens` estimate tokens? Is it bytes/4?
questions.reference: estimateTokens (src/batch.zig), estimator zgrep-classes-v1: a weighted sum of bytes, digits, punctuation, whitespace runs and non-ASCII bytes, times a scale (1.112*1.01), calibrated against a real BPE so it does not underestimate. It replaced bytes/4, which underestimated.

questions.question: Which event types count as results for `--max-results`? Do context lines count?
questions.reference: isResult (src/batch.zig): match, occurrence, file and count events. Context, passthru, provenance, query_end and summary do not count.

questions.question: When does `zgrep --cache` consider a Zig cache in use (ACTIVA), and how does it recognise a Zig compiler process?
questions.reference: procsHomeActive (src/clean.zig), Linux only, through /proc: the global cache is active if any live zig process exists anywhere; a local cache is active if some zig process has its cwd inside the repository that contains it. A process counts only if the basename of /proc/<pid>/exe is exactly zig (a ' (deleted)' suffix is stripped). Lock files (any name containing 'lock') are also checked.

questions.question: Does `zgrep --cache` delete `zig-out` directories?
questions.reference: Not by default. Only with --include-out, and even then a zig-out is protected (PROTEGIDA) if a symlink in a well-known bin directory points inside it (hasInstallLink, src/clean.zig). Symlinks themselves are never deleted, and the default answer to the prompt is N.

questions.question: What values does `--encoding` accept, and what does `--encoding=utf-16` do with a file that has no BOM?
questions.reference: parseEncoding (src/scan.zig): auto, none, utf-8, utf-16, utf-16le, utf-16be, latin1. auto = BOM sniff only (default); utf-16le/be decode ignoring any BOM; utf-16 lets the BOM decide and falls back to little-endian (like rg); utf-8/latin1 use the bytes as they are.

questions.question: In a `--provenance` event, what values can "source" take, and when is it "file-utf16"?
questions.reference: ProvSource (src/scan.zig): file, file-utf16, pre, stdin. provSourceOf returns file-utf16 when the file is decoded as UTF-16: a forced utf-16le/utf-16be, --encoding=utf-16, or a UTF-16 BOM detected; with --encoding=none it is always file.

questions.question: With `--crlf`, is the trailing `\r` printed, and does a CRLF count as one line terminator or two?
questions.reference: visibleLineEnd (src/scan.zig) returns the position of the \n minus the \r when --crlf is on, so the \r is not part of the printed line; lines are split on \n, so a CRLF is one terminator (a past bug counted it twice and numbered matches 1, 3, 5...).

questions.question: Does `zgrep -i 'ñand.'` match the line `ÑANDÚ`? Does the README's statement that `-i` folds the Latin-1 supplement hold for regular expressions?
questions.reference: No. Latin-1 folding only exists in the literal search path (isCaseFoldable/toLowerByte in src/search.zig). The regex engine folds ASCII only (byteSet and the class folding in src/regex.zig touch only a-z/A-Z; its header says '-i folds ASCII only'). `ñand.` contains a metacharacter, so it goes through the regex engine and does not match ÑANDÚ, while the plain literal `ñandú` does. The README's claim holds only for literal patterns.

questions.question: Are `\b` word boundaries supported in zgrep regular expressions? The header comment of src/regex.zig lists `\b` as not supported.
questions.reference: Yes, \b and \B are supported: the parser's error message says 'back-references and lookaround are not supported; \b and \B ARE', and README/--help document them. The header comment in src/regex.zig (around line 17) is stale. Back-references and lookaround are rejected with an error.

questions.question: What happens when the lazy DFA's state cache fills up during a search?
questions.reference: At max_states = 3000 (src/regex.zig) the DFA cache is flushed (reset) and interning starts over; the comment warns callers not to reuse old state ids. The search continues: there is no error and no fallback to a separate NFA mode.

questions.question: What makes a directory tree a "micro-tree" in zgrep, and what changes when it is one?
questions.reference: Its regular files add up to less than 2 MB (micro_tree_max_bytes = 2*1024*1024 in src/main.zig) and the discovery stays within 2048 files, 512 directories and depth 32 (tryQuickTreeScan, src/kamikaze.zig). It is scanned on the calling thread: no worker pool, no io_uring, and no .gitignore/.dataignore inspection. --force-swarm disables the micro path.

questions.question: Before starting worker threads in `-q` mode, how many files does zgrep probe, and where?
questions.reference: Up to 4 regular files in the root directory, on the main thread, before the thread pool is created (tryQuickQuietProbe, src/kamikaze.zig: `while (probed < 4)`). The README's Design section says three files, which contradicts the code.

questions.question: What does `zgrep --nav 'v^v' needle dir/` search?
questions.reference: Nothing. NavPlan.parse (src/nav.zig) sets has_ceiling for the `v^` pair and has_trampoline for the `^v` pair. shouldScanFiles returns false at depth 0 (trampoline) and shouldRecurseSubdirs always returns false (ceiling), so no file is searched and the run exits 1 with no message.

questions.question: Does zgrep accept `--binary-files=binary`? What do `text` and `without-match` do?
questions.reference: No: `binary` is rejected at parse time with a usage error, because zgrep cannot print matches while suppressing binary content (BinaryFiles in src/main.zig). `text` is exactly -a; `without-match` is the default (a binary file is treated as not matching).

questions.question: With `-S` (smart case) and the all-lowercase pattern `ñandú`, does zgrep search case-insensitively?
questions.reference: No. The uppercase check (src/main.zig, after parsing) treats raw bytes 0xC0..0xDE (except 0xD7) as Latin-1 uppercase. In UTF-8 the lead byte of ñ and ú is 0xC3, which is in that range, so the lowercase pattern counts as having an uppercase letter and the search stays case-sensitive (ÑANDÚ is not found; rg -S finds it).

questions.question: What does `--color=auto` do in zgrep?
questions.reference: It degrades to never: zgrep does not check isatty(stdout) (ColorMode, src/main.zig: 'auto degrades to never off a TTY'; help: 'auto = never'), so auto never colours.

questions.question: How does `--exec` interact with ordering, `-q`-style early exit, `--json` and `--queries-file` batches?
questions.reference: --exec forces the sorted (ordered) path and runs the commands after the scan; it sets quiet mode but keeps the quiet early-exits off so every matching file is reached; --json with --exec is a usage error; --exec is not allowed in a batch. {} in the command is the path, otherwise the path is appended.

questions.question: Which options make zgrep use the sorted (ordered) path even when `--sort` is not given?
questions.reference: --exec, --heading and --pre each set opts.sort = true in runSearch (src/main.zig): exec needs to know which files matched, heading groups would interleave in completion order, and --pre runs per file.

questions.question: If binary data that does NOT contain the pattern is piped into zgrep on standard input, what does zgrep print and with what exit code?
questions.reference: It prints 'Binary file (standard input) matches' and exits 0 anyway: in the stdin path of runSearch (src/main.zig ~2295) a NUL in the first binary_probe_bytes (8192) makes is_bin true and the code prints the message and returns 0 without searching. GNU grep exits 1. A binary FILE is handled correctly.

questions.question: What units does `--max-filesize` accept, are they powers of 1000 or 1024, and what is the default?
questions.reference: parseSize (src/main.zig): an optional leading '+', a number, and an optional suffix k/K, m/M, g/G, t/T in powers of 1024 (no suffix = bytes); the multiplication saturates. The default is 0, which means unlimited.

questions.question: Is there a hard limit on directory depth in zgrep even without `--max-depth`?
questions.reference: Yes in the sorted walk: walk_max_depth = 512 (src/walk.zig); going deeper returns error.TooDeep. (The micro path additionally gives up at depth 32 and hands the tree to the swarm.) --max-depth=0 means no user limit.

questions.question: For a UTF-16 file with `--json --provenance`, does sha256 hash the raw file or the decoded text, what do the offsets refer to, and what is mtime_ns for standard input?
questions.reference: The hash is of the bytes zgrep read and searched (not a re-read); for file-utf16 the hash is of the raw file while the offsets refer to the decoded text; mtime_ns comes from statx and is null when there is no file (stdin); for --pre the hash is of the preprocessor output (out_json.zig emitProvenanceEvent doc).

questions.question: What does `--stop-on-nonmatch` do in zgrep, and where is it implemented?
questions.reference: Nothing: it is parsed (src/main.zig ~1267), stored in Options and copied into ScanConfig.stop_on_nonmatch, but no code in src/scan.zig (or anywhere else) ever reads it, so it has no effect: `a1 a2 b a3` still prints a3 (rg stops after a2). The --help text describes a behaviour that is not implemented.

questions.question: Does `zgrep -t docker` search a file named exactly `Dockerfile`?
questions.reference: No. The type registry (src/types.zig) lists "Dockerfile" among the docker extensions; applyTypes passes it to addIncludedExts, and matchesExt (src/filter.zig) for an extension without a leading dot requires a longer name with a '.' right before it. A file named exactly Dockerfile does not match (app.Dockerfile would); rg -t docker does find it.

questions.question: What peak resident memory (RSS) does zgrep reach when searching a single 4 GB file, and how long does that take on an NVMe drive?
questions.reference: Not answerable from the repository: there is no RSS or timing measurement for a 4 GB file. The code only shows that files of at least mmap_threshold (256 KB, src/scan.zig) are memory-mapped, so RSS depends on the page cache. A correct answer says the information is not available.
